title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the previous one, 'Calcul des Ext^i(G_a,G_a)'. It works in sheaves of F_p-modules on a big site over a field k of characteristic p (the perfect site is mentioned on the previous page). Its content is very close to Lawrence Breen's computation of the Yoneda groups Ext^i(G_a,G_a) and his vanishing theorem on the perfect site, which Milne needed for flat duality. It may be Grothendieck's notes from a talk by Breen, or his own working-through of Breen's method.

Structure.
(1) Universal coefficient spectral sequence E_2^{i,j} = Ext^i(H_j(K(G_a,n)), G_a) ⇒ H^{i+j}(K(G_a,n), G_a). The argument is an induction on i, carried out modulo F-torsion in the sense of a Serre class C. This uses the stable range (n large), where H_j(K(G_a,n)) = 0 for 0<j<n and H_n = G_a.
(2) The low-degree exact sequence of edge maps reads Ext^i(H_n, G_a) → H^{n+i}(K(G_a,n),G_a) → Hom(H_{n+i}(K(G_a,n)),G_a) → Ext^{i+1}(G_a,G_a) →∂ H^{n+i+1}(K(G_a,n),G_a). Because of the vanishing range, Ext^i(G_a,G_a) sits in this sequence.
(3) Lemma 1 states that the edge homomorphism ∂ is zero. The proof is by comparison with the constant groups F_{p^h}, where Ext^{i+1}_{F_p}(F_{p^h},F_{p^h}) = 0 among F_p-vector spaces.
(4) Lemma 2 identifies the generators. Hom(H_{n+i}(K(G_a,n)),G_a) ≅ Hom(G_a ⊗ H_{n+i}(K(F_p,n)), G_a) ≅ H^{n+i}(K(F_p,n),F_p) ⊗ Hom(G_a,G_a). Its generators are admissible Steenrod monomials P^I ι_n, including Bockstein-type terms. The key point is that P^d ι_n corresponds to P^d ι_n ⊗ F (a Frobenius twist). The proof reduces to the case P^0 ι_n.
(5) The stated answer: Ext^{2i+1}(G_a,G_a) = 0 for i>0, and Ext^{2i}(G_a,G_a) = k[F]/(F^α) with α = v_p(i). In particular these groups are F-torsion, so they vanish after perfection.
(6) The second method is a stable, Mac Lane-style one. Iterated suspensions Σ^j K(G_a,n) give a spectral sequence Ext^i(Σ^j K(G_a,n), G_a) ⇒ Ext^{i+j}(G_a,G_a), using Σ[Σ^{j-1}K] ~ Σ[K(Z)∧…∧K(Z)∧K(G_a,n)].
- The E_1 term, via Künneth, is a cobar-type complex built from the Steenrod algebra A = H^*(K(F_p),F_p) and the 'G_a-Steenrod algebra' 𝒜 = H^*(K(G_a),G_a), with the coproduct P^i ↦ Σ P^j⊗P^k.
- Dually, E_2 = Tor^{A_*}(𝒜_*, F_p), which is computed by a Koszul complex.
This is Breen's strategy in 'Extensions du groupe additif' (Publ. IHES 48, 1978).
errors: The formula Ext^{2i}(G_a,G_a) = k[F]/(F^α) with α = v_p(i) would make Ext^{2i} vanish whenever p does not divide i. That gives Ext^2 = 0, which looks suspicious compared with Breen's published answer (a nonzero F-torsion module in even degrees). The exponent may be misremembered or miscopied, for example v_p(i)+1 or an indexing shift. I cannot confirm this.
Lemma 1 is justified only by a sketchy comparison diagram with F_{p^h}; how this transfers to G_a (passage to the limit, compatibility of ∂) is not written out.
The working assumption 'mod F' (Serre-class arguments) is used without checking that the class of F-torsion k[F]-modules is closed under the needed operations (extensions, Ext with G_a).

ideas.what: Computation of Ext^i(G_a,G_a) in sheaves of F_p-modules via the universal coefficient spectral sequence for K(G_a,n) and Steenrod operations
ideas.usually_credited_to: L. Breen, Extensions du groupe additif, Publ. Math. IHES 48 (1978)

ideas.what: Ext^i(G_a^parf, G_a^parf) = 0 for i>0 on the perfect site, since the higher Ext groups are F-torsion
ideas.modern_name: Breen's vanishing theorem on the perfect site (used in Milne's flat duality)
ideas.usually_credited_to: L. Breen, 'Extensions du groupe additif sur le site parfait' (LNM 868, 1981); motivated by J. Milne

ideas.what: Stable approach: E_2 = Tor^{A_*}(𝒜_*, F_p), where 𝒜 is the G_a-coefficient Steenrod algebra (A twisted by Frobenius), computed by a Koszul complex
ideas.modern_name: Mac Lane / cobar spectral sequence for stable Ext; precursor of functor-cohomology computations (Franjou–Lannes–Schwartz, Friedlander–Suslin)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Breen (1978); later functor-category versions by Franjou–Lannes–Schwartz (1994) and Friedlander–Suslin (1997)

deep.surprise_reason: The page appears to be lecture or reading notes reproducing Breen's known method and results on Ext(G_a,G_a). Breen's paper is well cited, and its link to functor cohomology is already in the literature. Nothing appears new; the only oddity is a possibly misremembered exponent formula.
transcription_corrections: Previous page: 'est de F lorscon' should read 'est de F-torsion'.
The isomorphism under Hom(H_{n+i}(K(G_a,n)),G_a) reads roughly '⊕ Hom(F_α, G_a)' (a direct sum of Hom groups), not 'Hom(...,G_a)'.
'ξ P^{i_1}…P^{i_n} ι_n' is probably 'β^{ε} P^{i_1}…P^{i_k} ι_n' (admissible monomials with Bocksteins); 'longueur n+s' refers to the degree or length of the monomial.
The 'E^2 par Koszul' at the end is 'E_2 = Tor^{A_*}(𝒜_*, F_p) ⇒ E_2 par Koszul', i.e. computed via a Koszul resolution.
